exam: Microsoft 98-382: Introduction to Programming Using JavaScript
format: Non-MC questions use `blanks` (one per dropdown / drop target). A blank is placed either inline in `template` via {{n}} or as a labelled row in `rows`. `answer` is the PDF answer key. `note` flags where the PDF key disagrees with how JavaScript actually behaves.

questions.prompt:
You are creating a web page that tests a user's ability to accurately type text. The validation should be case-insensitive.

How should you complete the code? Drag appropriate functions to the correct locations. Each function may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
questions.template: When in the course of human events...
questions.explanation:
An exposes what the user typed through .value; a

exposes its text through .innerHTML.
questions.note: The PDF key fills the if-statement with value / innerHTML. That doesn't work: input and text are already strings, so input.value and text.innerHTML are both undefined and the test always passes. For a case-insensitive check, the if-statement should be input.toLowerCase() == text.toLowerCase().

questions.explanation: An unassigned variable is undefined. "3.4" is a string. 2.4 is a number. typeof null is "object" (a long-standing quirk of the language).

questions.prompt:
You are writing an engineering application. You need to create a function that will round numbers to 3 or more decimal places.

The function receives two parameters:
• value: the number to be formatted
• digits: the number of digits to display

The function must return the value with the number of digits specified. Which function should you use?
questions.explanation: toFixed(digits) formats a number with exactly that many digits after the decimal point. toPrecision counts total significant digits, toString(digits) treats the argument as a radix (base), and valueOf ignores its argument.

questions.prompt:
You analyze the following code fragment. Line numbers are included for reference only.

For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
rows: The call to the multiply function on line 09 returns 100.
The call to the multiply function on line 19 returns 100.
questions.explanation: Line 09 calls the global multiply, which uses the global values 25 * 4 = 100. Line 19 calls the inner multiply, which uses the local values 2 * 3 = 6.

questions.prompt:
You are creating a JavaScript function that returns a date the specified number of months in the future of the current date.

The function must:
• Accept a number that represents the number of months to add or subtract from the current date.
• Return the current date adjusted by the number of months passed into the function.

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: new Date() creates a Date object for now (Date() without new returns a string). getMonth() and setMonth() are methods, so they must be called on the date object with parentheses. setMonth handles year rollover automatically.

questions.prompt:
You work as a JavaScript developer for Adventure Works. You are writing a simple script that:
• Declares and initializes an array
• Fills the array with 10 random integers
• Adds every other number starting with the first element

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: [] creates an empty array literal and push() appends each random integer.
questions.note: The PDF key's last two answers are wrong. j = j++ assigns the old value back to j, so the loop never ends. To add every other element, use j = j+2. There is no variable named array, so the sum must use numbers[j].

questions.prompt:
You are creating JavaScript code that manipulates dates. You want to initialize a Date object with the date January 1, 2017 by using the year, month, and date parameters.

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: Use the full 4-digit year (a 2-digit year is read as 19xx). Months are zero-based (January = 0), but the day of the month starts at 1.

questions.prompt:
Your instructor has asked you to write a program that uses simple rules to help determine if a person should take the train, drive their car, or ride a bike, depending on the weather and the amount of gas in the car's tank.

Requirements:
• When the temperature is above 65 degrees and it is not raining, the person should be told to ride their bike.
• When it is raining, the person should be told to drive their car.
• If their car has half a tank of gas or less, they should be told to take the train.

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: Both conditions (warm AND not raining) must hold, so use logical AND (&&). "Half a tank or less" means fuelTank <= .5.

questions.prompt:
You are using JavaScript to create a function that calculates admission price.

Requirements:
• The function accepts the age of the customer as a parameter
• A customer who is less than 5 years old gets in free
• A customer who is 65 years old or older gets in free
• A customer who is 5 to 17 years old pays $10 USD
• All other customers pay $20 USD

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: Free entry applies to either group (under 5 OR 65 and over), so use ||. The $10 band must satisfy both bounds (5 or older AND under 18), so use &&.

questions.prompt:
The ABC company offers a mid-week discount of 10% on Wednesdays. You need to write a JavaScript function that:
• Accepts the day of the week as a string
• Returns the appropriate discount

You must complete the code at lines 03, 04, and 07.
questions.explanation: A switch statement tests day; case "Wednesday": handles the discount day; default: handles every other day.

questions.prompt:
You are creating a function named countdown. The function accepts a single parameter, start, and displays a countdown from that number down to zero in increments of one.

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: Start i at start and decrement with --i after each pass.
questions.note: The PDF key picks i>0, which stops at 1 and never prints 0. To count down to zero, the condition must be i>=0.

questions.prompt:
You are creating a calendar application. You need to ensure that the code works correctly for all months of the year.

How should you complete the code?
questions.explanation: switch (month) selects the case. Each case must end with break; so it does not fall through into the next case.
questions.note: The PDF key picks continue; after case 1. That is a SyntaxError here, because continue is only valid inside a loop. The correct answer is break;.

questions.prompt:
You are creating a function that does safe division.

Requirements:
• The function receives two parameters for the numerator and denominator.
• If the denominator is zero, the function must return false.
• If the denominator is not zero, the function must return true.

You write the following code. For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
rows: The function will always return false.
The operator at line 02 should be !=
questions.explanation: denominator = 0 is an assignment, and its value 0 is falsy, so the function always returns true, not false. The operator should be == (or ===), not !=.

questions.prompt:
Variable x has a value of 5. Variable y has a value of 7.

For each expression, select True if it evaluates to true. Otherwise, select False.
questions.explanation: 5 < 7 && 7 > 6 is true. 5 == 6 || 7 == 6 is false. 5 !== 7 is true. 5 == 7 is false, so !(false) is true.

questions.prompt:
You are developing a web page that uses JavaScript. The script needs to display information to the user using a popup box.

Match each function that displays a popup box with its appropriate scenario. Each function may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
rows: Display a dialog box that allows the user to enter a street address.
Display an error message using a function that does not return a value.
Display a dialog box and return a value indicating which button the user clicked.
questions.explanation: prompt() returns the text the user typed. alert() only shows a message and returns undefined. confirm() returns true (OK) or false (Cancel).

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Code that might throw goes in a try block. catch (err) runs only when an exception is thrown. finally would run every time.
